description: Export corridors: two competing logistics systems
verification_status: confirmed by multiple sources (Reuters/Ecofin, OECD, ORF, Veracity Worldwide, AFC)
key_paradox: Lobito is Western-financed, but its biggest potential customers are Chinese-capitalized mines. The open-access model can't exclude Chinese companies without undermining the project's economics. At the same time, CMOC and Zijin have taken equity stakes in the competing TAZARA line - hedging both routes.

corridors.name: Lobito Corridor
corridors.direction: west, to the Atlantic (Port of Lobito, Angola)
corridors.operator: Lobito Atlantic Railway - a consortium of Trafigura (49.5%), Mota-Engil, and Vecturis; 30-year concession
corridors.length_km: 1,300+ (rehabilitation of the Benguela railway) plus ~830 km of new line through Zambia
corridors.2026_financing: a $753m financing package closed (Africa Finance Corporation, July 2026); ~$1bn previously mobilized via PGII
corridors.speed: 5-8 days from Kolwezi to the Atlantic versus ~25 days by road to Durban
corridors.drc_commitment: reportedly, 50% of DRC state companies' copper, 30% of cobalt, and 90% of zinc must move via the DRC section within the next 5 years
corridors.risks: the DRC section is badly degraded; the Zambian extension has not started; questions about economic viability (ECDPM, IRIS); no supranational governance body

corridors.name: TAZARA (Tanzania-Zambia)
corridors.direction: east, to the Indian Ocean (Port of Dar es Salaam)
corridors.structural_significance: vertical integration: extraction (CMOC, Zijin) + inland logistics (Jiayou) + sea transport (COSCO) in one loop
corridors.throughput_target: growth from 100,000 t to 2.4 million t per year
corridors.current_state: annual throughput ~230,000 t, after decades of underinvestment

player_shares_of_2025_drc_exports.Zijin: 39.6% stake in Kamoa-Kakula - the country's largest copper complex

conclusion: This isn't a simple either/or contest, it's a split by destination: Lobito targets Atlantic (Western) markets, TAZARA targets Asian and Chinese processing capacity. For Kinshasa and Lusaka, simply having two competing sponsors creates a bargaining leverage that would not exist with only one.
